source_text: Quonram autem non indigens Deus servitute eorum, sed propter ipsos quasdam observantias in lege praeceperit, plenissime prophetz indicant. Et rursus quoniam non indiget Deus oblatione eorum, sed propter ipsum qui offerat hominem, manifeste Dominus docuit, quemadmodum ostendimus. Si quando enim negligentes eos justitiam, et abstinentes a dilectione Dei videbat, per sacrificia autem et reliquas typicas observantias putantes propitiari Deum, dicebat eis Samuel quidem sic; Non vult Deus holocausta et sacrificia, sed vult exaudiri vocem suam. Ecce, auditus bonus super sacrificium, et auditus super adipem arietum. David autem ait: Sacrificium et oblationem noluisti ; ®aures autem perfecisti mihi: holocausta etiam pro delicto non postulasti. Docens eos quoniam obauditionem vult Deus, que servat eos, quam sacrificia et holocaustomata, que nihil eis prosunt ad justitiam : et novum simul prophetans Testamentum. Manifestius autem adhue in quinquagesimo Psalmo de his ait: Quoniam si voluisses sacrificium, dedissem utique: holocaustis non delectaberis. Sacrificiwm Deo spiritus contribulatus Quoniam ergo nihil et humiliatum Dominus non despernet. indiget Deus, in eo qui est ante hune Psalmo ait: Non accipiam de domo tua vitulos, nec de gregibus tuis hircos. sunt omnes bestiw terra, jumenta in montibus et boves; cognovi omnia volatilia coli, et species agri mecum est. dicam tibi : meus est enim orbis terra, et plenitudo ejus. Nunquid manducabo carnes taurorum, aut sanguinem hircorum potabo? Deinde ne quis putet, propterea quod irasceretur, eum recusare infert, consilium ei dans: Jmmola Deo sacrificium laudis, et redde Altissimo vota tua, et invoca me in die tribulationis tuce, et eripiam te, et glorificabis me; illa quidem per que putabant peccantes propitiari Deum abnuens, et ostendens quod ipse nullius rei indiget ; ®heee autem per que justificatur homo, et appropinDeo, hortatur et admonet. 2. Hoc idem autem et Esaias ait: Quo mihi multitudinem sacrificiorum vestrorum, dicit Dominus? Plenus sum. Et cum abnuisset holocaustomata, et sacrificia, et oblationes, et adhuc neomenias, et sabbata, et ferias, et reliquam universam consequentem his observationem, intulit, suadens eis que salutaria sunt: Lavamini, mundi estote, auferte nequitias a cordibus. vestris ab oculis meis: desinite a malitiis vestris, discite bonum facere, exquirite judicium, eruite eum qui injuriam patitur, judicate pupillo, et justificate viduam, et venite disputemus, dicit Dominus. Non enim sicut homo motus, ut multi audent dicere, divertit eorum sacrificia; sed miserans eorum cexcitati, et verum sacrificium insinuans, quod offerentes propitiabuntur Deum, ut ab eo vitam percipiant.
pass_a_gloss: For since God not needing their service, but on account of them having commanded certain observances in the law, the prophets indicate very fully. And again, since God does not need their offering, but on account of the one who offers, the man, the Lord has taught clearly, as we show. For when He saw them neglecting justice and abstaining from the love of God, and thinking to propitiate God through sacrifices and other typical observances, Samuel said to them thus: God does not want holocausts and sacrifices, but wants to hear His voice. Behold, obedience is better than sacrifice, and hearing than the fat of rams. And David says: You did not want sacrifice and offering; ears You have prepared for me; holocausts also for sin You did not ask. Teaching them that God wants obedience, which saves them, rather than sacrifices and holocausts, which do them no good for justice; and at the same time prophesying the New Testament. But more clearly still, in the fiftieth Psalm, He says about these things: For if You had wanted sacrifice, I would have given it; You are not delighted with holocausts. A sacrifice to God is a spirit crushed; for God does not despise a humble and contrite heart. Since therefore God needs nothing, in the Psalm before this one He says: I will not take from Your house bullocks, nor from Your flocks goats; for all the beasts of the earth are Mine, and the cattle on the mountains, and the oxen; I know all the birds of the air, and the species of the field are with Me. I will say to You: the earth is Mine, and the fullness of it. Shall I eat the flesh of bullocks, or drink the blood of goats? Then, lest anyone think that He rejects these things because He is angry, He gives them counsel: Offer to God a sacrifice of praise, and pay to the Most High Your vows, and call upon Me in the day of Your tribulation, and I will deliver You, and You will glorify Me; indeed, those things by which they thought to propitiate God, sinning, He rejects, and shows that He needs nothing; but those things by which man is justified and draws near to God, He exhorts and admonishes. And Isaiah says the same thing: What is the multitude of Your sacrifices to Me, says the Lord? I am full. And when He had rejected holocausts, and sacrifices, and offerings, and new moons, and sabbaths, and festivals, and the whole consequent observation of these things, He introduced, advising them of the things that are salutary: Be washed, be clean, remove wickedness from Your hearts, from before My eyes; cease from Your malices, learn to do good, seek judgment, rescue the one who suffers injury, judge for the orphan, and justify the widow, and come, let us dispute, says the Lord. For He does not turn away their sacrifices like a man moved, as many dare to say, but having mercy on their excitement, and insinuating the true sacrifice, which those offering will propitiate God, so that they may receive life from Him.

pass_b_english: The prophets make it perfectly clear that God commanded certain observances in the law not because He needs our service, but for our own sake. The Lord has taught the same truth just as plainly: He does not need our offerings, but accepts them for the sake of the one who offers them. When He saw His people neglecting justice and turning away from the love of God, yet imagining they could appease Him through sacrifices and other ceremonial observances, Samuel told them: "God does not want burnt offerings and sacrifices, but wants you to listen to His voice. Obedience is better than sacrifice, and to listen is better than the fat of rams" (1 Sam 15:22). David says the same: "You did not want sacrifice and offering, but You have given me an open ear. You did not ask for burnt offerings and sin offerings" (Ps 40:6). He was teaching them that God desires obedience, which saves them, rather than sacrifices and burnt offerings, which do nothing to make them just—and in saying this he was also prophesying the New Testament. The fiftieth Psalm states this even more clearly: "If You had wanted sacrifice, I would have given it; You take no delight in burnt offerings. The sacrifice acceptable to God is a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart, O God, You will not despise" (Ps 51:16-17). Since God needs nothing, the preceding Psalm declares: "I will not accept a bull from your house, or goats from your folds. For every beast of the forest is Mine, the cattle on a thousand hills. I know all the birds of the air, and all that moves in the field is Mine. If I were hungry, I would not tell you, for the world and its fullness are Mine. Do I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats?" (Ps 50:9-13). Then, so that no one would think He rejects these things out of anger, He gives them counsel: "Offer to God a sacrifice of thanksgiving, and pay your vows to the Most High. Call upon Me in the day of trouble; I will deliver you, and you shall glorify Me" (Ps 50:14-15). He rejects the very things by which sinners thought they could appease Him, showing that He needs nothing; but He urges and admonishes them toward the things by which a person is justified and draws near to God. Isaiah says the same: "What to Me is the multitude of your sacrifices? says the Lord; I have had enough of burnt offerings of rams and the fat of well-fed beasts" (Is 1:11). After rejecting burnt offerings, sacrifices, grain offerings, new moons, Sabbaths, festivals, and the whole train of observances that follow them, He points them to what truly saves: "Wash yourselves; make yourselves clean; remove the evil of your deeds from before My eyes; cease to do evil, learn to do good; seek justice, correct oppression; bring justice to the fatherless, plead the widow's cause. Come now, let us reason together, says the Lord" (Is 1:16-18). He does not turn away their sacrifices like a man moved by emotion, as many dare to claim, but in mercy toward their misguided zeal He points them to the true sacrifice—one which, when offered, propitiates God so that they may receive life from Him.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A preserves the clause structure and nuances of the Latin (e.g., 'on account of them' for 'propter ipsos'). Pass B provides a fluent English rendering with appropriate scripture citations (1 Sam 15:22, Ps 40:6, Ps 51:16-17, Ps 50:9-13, Ps 50:14-15, Is 1:11, Is 1:16-18) that correspond to the quoted content. The title 'God's Desire for Obedience' correctly names the thought of the passage.
